rationale: Tests recognition of the pathognomonic lesion (burrow) and scabies predilection sites, completing the learning point on clinical presentation established in block 3.

Tests recognition of crusted (Norwegian) scabies and its management implications in an immunocompromised patient, anchored after block 5 which establishes diagnostic features including crusted scabies.
Tests the key distributional distinction between scabies and its closest mimic (atopic dermatitis), anchored after block 7 which establishes the differential diagnosis.

Tests the ability to devise a safe, complete treatment plan for scabies in pregnancy — the core of competency DR5.1 — anchored after block 8 which establishes scabicide choices, ADRs, and contact management.

Tests visual recognition of the three louse types and their characteristic habitats, anchored after block 3 which establishes the morphological and site-based distinctions among pediculosis capitis, corporis, and pubis.
Tests recall of the louse life-cycle stages in correct chronological order, anchored after block 4 which establishes the complete life cycle and its clinical significance.

Tests the ability to diagnose pediculosis corporis when lice are absent from the skin and to recall the body louse's vector role, anchored after block 5 which establishes diagnostic methods including clothing-seam examination.
Tests the key bedside distinction between nits and dandruff — the most common diagnostic confusion in pediculosis capitis — anchored after block 7 which establishes the differential diagnosis.

Tests the management of treatment-resistant pediculosis capitis including second-line agent selection and abandonment of outdated no-nit exclusion policies, anchored after block 8 which establishes management including resistance patterns.
